overview.headline: A vendor-designed variant of semax with no published research of its own.
overview.lede: Adamax is sold by online "research chemical" shops as a longer-acting version of the Russian nasal drug semax. It has no manufacturer of record, no regulator has ever reviewed it, and we could find no peer-reviewed study of it in animals or people as of October 2026. Everything said about it is borrowed from semax or asserted by sellers.

mechanism.intro: Sellers describe Adamax as semax with two chemical add-ons copied from another research peptide, P21.

parts.name: Semax core
parts.text: The seven amino acids of semax, an ACTH fragment approved in Russia as nasal drops for stroke and cognitive complaints. Semax's own evidence is Russian and unblinded; see its page.

parts.name: The add-ons
parts.text: An acetyl cap at one end and an adamantane-bearing glycine at the other, said to slow breakdown and help the molecule cross into the brain. That is a chemist's expectation. No published study has tested whether Adamax does either.

more.title: More: where it comes from
paras: No scientist, institute or company has published a description of Adamax. It appeared in online peptide catalogues in recent years, sometimes listed as "Adamax 1032" after its molecular weight. New Zealand's medicines regulator, Medsafe, described it in 2025 as an ACTH analogue marketed with nootropic claims whose mechanism is unknown and whose clinical research is limited.
This page therefore has little to report. Where we describe effects, they belong to semax, not Adamax, and we say so.

results.headline: There are no results. Nobody has studied it.
results.lede: A search of the medical literature in October 2026 found no human trial, no animal study and no laboratory paper on Adamax. The claims on vendor pages (sharper focus, longer action, more BDNF) are marketing, resting on studies of semax.

stats.lbl: human participants ever reported to have received Adamax in a study

items.t: Nothing. There are no studies to show anything.
Thirteen unblinded Russian stroke studies and small case series for cognitive complaints. No placebo-controlled trial. Whether any of this carries over to a chemically different molecule is unknown.

items.b: P21, the source of the add-ons.
items.t: The acetyl cap and adamantylated glycine were used by a New York lab to make a different peptide (from a nerve growth factor) that works in mice. That says nothing about what the same chemistry does to semax.
None. Adamax is not on the FDA's compounding list in any category and appears in no regulator's documents except as a border-seizure item in New Zealand.

more.title: More: why "it is just semax plus a bit" is not evidence
paras: Small changes to a peptide can change how it binds, how long it lasts and what it breaks down into. Drug developers test every such variant from scratch. For Adamax, no one has done even the first step of showing the product sold is the molecule described.

effects.headline: Unknown. No study has recorded a single side effect, or a single safe exposure.
effects.lede: Because no one has given Adamax to people or animals under observation, there is no side-effect profile. Reports on forums are unverifiable and tell you nothing about what was actually in the vial.

disc.title: Stopping because of side effects
disc.text: Not reported. There are no trials.

unique.title: What has actually been reported
unique.text: Nothing in the scientific literature. The only official document naming Adamax, the 2025 Medsafe submission, says its side effects are poorly understood. Semax's Russian label excludes people with anxiety disorders, psychosis or a history of seizures, which is the closest thing to a safety signal for this chemical family.

more.title: More: what the trials monitor for
paras: There are no trials. If one were ever run, it would start with animal toxicology, then a small human study measuring blood levels, immune reactions to the peptide, heart rate, blood pressure and mood. None of that exists.

more.title: More: the good side effects
paras: None documented. Claims of better focus or mood come from sellers and users, not from any measurement.

urgent.title: Symptoms trial teams treat as urgent
items: Swelling of the face or throat, hives or trouble breathing after a dose
A seizure, severe agitation or psychotic symptoms
Fever, spreading redness or pus at an injection site
Chest pain, fainting or a racing heartbeat
urgent.note: Anyone with these symptoms should get medical care right away, whatever product they have used.

levels.nopk: No one has measured Adamax in blood, in any species. There is no half-life, no time to peak and no known dose, so there is nothing to model. Vendor claims that it lasts longer than semax are untested.

stats.lbl: published tests confirming that products sold as Adamax contain it

explain.t: The simulator needs a measured half-life and time to peak from a human study. Adamax has no study of any kind.

explain.b: Why semax's numbers cannot be borrowed.
explain.t: Semax has no published human half-life either, and the add-ons on Adamax are meant to change exactly the property a half-life measures.

explain.b: Why products sold online are a second unknown.
explain.t: Without a published analytical method, no buyer can confirm the contents of a vial labelled Adamax.

more.title: More: why there is no chart
paras: A pharmacokinetic chart is a summary of measurements. For Adamax there are none, so a chart would be fiction.

more.title: More: what a chart could not tell you anyway
paras: Even for well-studied drugs a blood-level curve says nothing about benefit or harm. Those questions need trials, and Adamax has had none.

trials.headline: No trial has ever been run, registered or announced.
trials.lede: There is no record of Adamax on ClinicalTrials.gov, the EU registry or any other public trial register, and no company has declared plans to study it.

more.title: More: what a first study would need
paras: Before a human trial, regulators require chemical characterisation of the molecule, stability data, and animal toxicology. None of this has been published for Adamax. A first-in-human study would then give single rising doses to a few healthy volunteers under hospital monitoring. Nothing on a vendor page resembles this.

running.title: Trials that have been run
items: None. No human or animal study of Adamax has been published (checked October 2026).
For context, the parent compound semax has 13 unblinded Russian stroke studies and no placebo-controlled trial; see the semax page.

find.text: There are no Adamax trials anywhere. The registry search below will show if that changes.

status.headline: Approved nowhere, assessed nowhere, sold anyway.

items.label: Canada
items.text: No Health Canada authorisation (no entry in the Drug Product Database, October 2026). Anything sold as Adamax in Canada is an unauthorised drug.

items.label: United States
items.text: Not approved. Adamax does not appear in any category of the FDA's compounding bulk-substances list (14 May 2026 version), so unlike semax it has no pending review. Selling it for human use is selling an unapproved new drug, whatever the label says.

items.label: New Zealand
items.text: Named by Medsafe in June 2025 as an ACTH analogue arriving in intercepted parcels; Medsafe proposed classifying it as a prescription medicine so that imports without a prescription can be stopped.

items.label: Sport
items.text: Not named on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List.

cards.title: What "research use only" means
cards.text: Adamax exists only as a "research chemical". The label is a legal device: by saying "not for human consumption", sellers try to stay outside drug law while marketing to people who intend to use it.
items: No regulator checks what is in the vial. For a compound with no published analytical method, not even the seller can prove it.
There is no safety data to fall back on. A doctor treating a reaction has nothing to look up.
Regulators in New Zealand and the U.S. treat such products as unapproved medicines regardless of the label.

cards.title: Symptoms to take to a doctor
cards.text: Anyone who has used a product sold as Adamax should see a doctor if they notice:
items: New anxiety, agitation, insomnia or mood change
Fever, redness or swelling at an injection site
cards.note: Bring the vial. Report a reaction to MedEffect Canada (canada.ca/medeffect) or, in the U.S., FDA MedWatch (fda.gov/medwatch).

more.title: More: the difference between semax and Adamax, legally
paras: Semax is a registered medicine in Russia and is under active review for U.S. compounding after a July 2026 advisory vote. Adamax is neither. Even if the FDA eventually lists semax, that listing would not extend to a chemically different molecule.
